Elena: Quick note from this morning's bring-up. We A/B'd a small ensemble (ranker-ensemble-v1: two models ensembled by score-avg) vs the current single best model (ranker-single-3b) on holdout-web-2026-07. NDCG_all +0.9 pts but MRR_top1 -1.4 pts. Pattern looks systematic — more top1 churn even though average ranks improved.

Kai: that's the classic ndcg vs top1 paradox. Do we have per-query histograms? Could be a few queries where the ensemble pushes a better overall ranking but demotes previous top1s.

Elena: pasted run summary: 
EvalBot: run-summary: run=6180204321 variants=[single,ensemble] ndcg_single=0.643 ndcg_ensemble=0.652 mrr_single=0.412 mrr_ensemble=0.398 seed=99 duration=1h22m

Jon: can you dump top-5 for queries where top1 flipped? Also confirm candidate pool parity and scoring determinism (same tokenization/padding).

Elena: candidate parity check returned OK (no doc id diffs). Tokenizer parity OK. I dumped top-5 diffs for top 200 queries by abs score delta. Snippet:

```
q: Q450
single_top5: [D2, D8, D15, D7, D3]
ensemble_top5: [D8, D2, D15, D7, D3]
scores_single: [0.91,0.90,0.88,0.85,0.82]
scores_ensemble: [0.92,0.89,0.88,0.85,0.82]
```
Many swaps like that. Top1 swapped from D2->D8. Ensemble slightly increased score for D8 but decreased for D2.

Sophie: are ensemble weights equal? averaging can prefer candidates with lower variance across models; that sometimes favors slightly different styles of documents. Could be dataset bias: web holdout has many short noisy snippets and the second model in the ensemble was trained with heavier short-doc augmentation.

Kai: good point. Check contribution per model: run the single models individually (A and B) and compare. If A had better top1 but B pulls up mid ranks, averaging might hurt top1.

EvalBot: run-started: 6180204330 variant=modelA_only

EvalBot: run-started: 6180204332 variant=modelB_only

Elena: results: modelA ndcg=0.642 mrr=0.415, modelB ndcg=0.639 mrr=0.392. Ensemble ndcg>both but mrr sits between A and B, closer to B. So ensemble improves average ranking but reduces top1 compared to A.

Jon: that's informative. Ensemble is balancing signals and smoothing extremes; when A had a stronger top1 signal, averaging penalizes that. For product surfaces where top1 matters (answer box), this is bad.

Sophie: actionable: 1) add metric-weighted ensemble: optimize ensemble weights for top1-sensitive objective (e.g., maximize MRR or a combined metric). 2) create per-query metric export so product teams can select ensemble variant by surface. 3) add a CI test that flags negative MRR deltas > 0.01 when ndcg improves by < 2 pts, to catch paradoxic regressions.

Elena: I ran a quick grid search for ensemble weights (wA from 0.0-1.0). Best MRR while keeping ndcg >= single was at wA=0.7 -> ndcg_ens=0.650 mrr_ens=0.410. Slight improvement over single mrr=0.412? actually it's still -0.002 relative; but much closer. Full grid results gist: https://gist.github.com/elena/ensemble-grid-weights

Kai: also consider rank-boost post-processing: if ensemble score for top candidate is within epsilon of single model's top, prefer single model decision for top1 to preserve high-precision picks. Simple rule: if score_diff < 0.015 then pick single_top1.

Jon: let's be careful with heuristics. Prefer to optimize weights per product surface. But as a stop-gap the epsilon rule could reduce top1 churn. Can someone run a validation with epsilon=0.015 and report ndcg/mrr?

EvalBot: run-started: 6180204340 variant=ensemble_epsilon015

Elena: quick result: ensemble+epsilon -> ndcg=0.651 mrr=0.409. Slightly better than plain ensemble, still marginally below single mrr but much closer.

Sophie: action items: Elena to attach per-query top-k diffs and grid results to the onboarding ticket. Kai to prototype metric-weighted optimizer for ensemble weights (objective: maximize weighted sum alpha*MRR + (1-alpha)*NDCG where alpha set by surface). Jon to propose CI gating rule for paradoxic regressions.

Elena: opened RNW-2102 and uploaded artifacts. I'll rerun full holdout with optimized weights for the search surface and include top1-preserving epsilon ablation.

Jon: great. Short-term: prefer single model for answer-box product where top1 matters; consider ensemble for feed/ranking surfaces where ndcg matters. Document in the bringup playbook.

EvalBot: note: per-query exports and the grid search gist uploaded to ticket RNW-2102. Closing thread for now.
